model_output.cross_horizon_summary: From the supplied issuance snapshot, downside has the stronger descriptive case over 12h and 72h, with MEDIUM confidence. The 168h horizon has NO_EDGE: current pressure does not establish a week-long decline, and selective resilience does not establish recovery. Positive transmission into altcoins remains weak and proxy-only. These are non-binding forecasts, not execution permissions; they do not alter framework thresholds or weights. The structural prior is context, not independent confirmation.
global_missing_evidence: Canonical broad-alt and large-cap breadth remain UNCONFIRMED; available breadth and capitalization measures are proxies.
Microcap transmission is unavailable. The small-alt proxy covers only the Top-100 tail, not the full small-cap universe.
No sustained multi-session price, ETH/BTC, breadth or flow sequence is supplied. Zero packet deltas do not establish market stability or independent persistence.
Catalyst context is degraded and supplies no usable forward event assessment; this is uncertainty, not bearish evidence.
Aggregate live-anchor source-observation freshness is unavailable, although component timestamps are supplied. Settled ETF, dominance and macro observations have different reporting lags.

contradicting_evidence: The BTC spot microstructure snapshot shows strong bid-side depth imbalance and positive taker imbalance, conflicting with the completed-hour selling pressure. These are different sampling windows, not proof of durable absorption.
BTC price and open interest both declined during the observed hour, consistent with some position reduction rather than uniformly expanding downside exposure.
Older capitalization proxies show selective altcoin resilience relative to BTC and ETH, although bucket median returns remained negative.
12h.expected_path: A choppy downside bias is more likely than sustained upside continuation. Brief rebounds are plausible around BTC bid support, but the supplied evidence does not establish recovery or broad participation.
falsification_conditions: Successive completed-hour gains accompanied by sustained spot buying and broader participation would weaken the downside forecast.
Persistent ETH/BTC strengthening together with improving ETH order flow and breadth would contradict the present weak-transmission setup.
missing_evidence: Persistence of order-book support and taker flow beyond the single microstructure snapshot.
A multi-hour price and open-interest sequence; the supplied hourly funding-event rates are unavailable, despite available live-anchor funding quotes.
Independent confirmation that broader participation improves alongside any rebound.
supporting_evidence: The freshest breadth proxy has 20 advancers and 79 decliners out of 100 constituents. It supersedes the older 35% advance-ratio snapshot rather than adding a separate vote.
Completed-hour BTC and ETH returns were approximately -0.21% and -0.27%, with taker-buy quote shares below one-half for both.
ETH price fell while open interest rose modestly; positive live-anchor funding and long-biased account ratios leave additional position-related vulnerability, without proving forced selling.
ETH order-book depth imbalance was strongly negative, and ETH/BTC showed no meaningful positive confirmation in the completed hour.

contradicting_evidence: Stablecoin supply contraction across the supplied daily, weekly and monthly windows provides a substantive downside lean.
Negative settled BTC and ETH ETF flows, weak current breadth and falling major-asset prices could persist into a broader decline.
There is no supplied confirmation of a sustained recovery to offset those pressures.
168h.expected_path: No defensible net-direction forecast is established for the full week. Renewed retests remain plausible, but stabilization, sustained recovery and continuing decline cannot be reliably sequenced from this snapshot. The weaker week-ahead conclusion does not imply an expected reversal of the shorter-horizon downside bias.
falsification_conditions: A sustained sequence of rising prices, strengthening ETH/BTC, source-qualified breadth expansion and improving flows would resolve uncertainty toward UP.
Persistent price deterioration accompanied by broad participation losses and continuing liquidity or flow contraction would resolve uncertainty toward DOWN.
missing_evidence: Subsequent settled ETF sessions and stablecoin observations showing whether contraction persists or reverses.
Durable, source-qualified breadth and relative-strength confirmation across several sessions.
A usable forward catalyst assessment and evidence of an established week-long price trend.
supporting_evidence: The evidence combines immediate selling pressure with selective relative resilience, without establishing which condition will dominate over a week.
Capitalization buckets outperforming falling BTC and ETH still have negative median returns; this distinguishes relative defense from absolute recovery.
Altseason readings are between published thresholds and do not confirm broad rotation.
A single settled dominance observation and isolated microstructure snapshots cannot establish a week-ahead transmission path.

contradicting_evidence: All observed large- and mid-alt proxy constituents outperformed BTC and ETH in the older snapshot, indicating relative resilience rather than indiscriminate underperformance.
BTC bid-side microstructure support could help interrupt the decline, but its durability is unverified.
Fear sentiment permits rebound risk but supplies no reliable turning-point signal.
72h.expected_path: Retests and failed stabilization attempts have a stronger evidence base than a durable recovery. A relief rebound could interrupt the decline; continuation would require price, participation and flows to improve together.
falsification_conditions: A sustained BTC and ETH recovery with improving ETH/BTC and durable breadth expansion would invalidate the downside bias.
Subsequent settled flows improving alongside price resilience and evidence of deployed liquidity would weaken the contraction thesis.
missing_evidence: Follow-through across several completed sessions rather than one hourly observation and isolated snapshots.
Newer settled ETF flows; the supplied final session is November 12 and does not describe subsequent demand.
An intraday or multi-day dominance trend and confirmed liquidity deployment.
supporting_evidence: Stablecoin supply declined approximately 0.45% over one day, 1.63% over seven days and 5.33% over thirty days; deployment confirmation is not established.
The latest supplied final ETF session recorded BTC outflows of $284.1 million and ETH outflows of $70.5 million.
The freshest breadth proxy is weak, while completed-hour BTC and ETH prices and ETH/BTC provide no positive follow-through confirmation.
Older large-, mid- and small-alt proxy median returns were negative despite substantial outperformance versus falling BTC and ETH; relative resilience is not broad recovery.
